scenario: AITA - Writing up a nurse | So I work in the ER- and a few weeks ago we had a larger patient in a room close to the nurses station. You can hear everything in that room that is said at the nurses station. The nurse taking care of him was one who I find immature and just an overall bad nurse. So this patient asked the nurse to be turned in the cart- our Er carts are small and uncomfortable. So the nurse comes out of the room and to the station and proceeds to say “alright I’m gonna need 12 people to help me with big boy down there.” “Alright sir, hold on I’m gonna need a fork lift.” To which I was appalled, at how inappropriate this nurse was. So normally I would tell the charge nurse but she was laughing along! So I texted my manager and they said they would take care of it. The nurse got written up. Well this week word got out I was the one who reported her and her and her catty friend group have been giving me shit all week. Am I the asshole?

- Healthcare workers have an ethical duty to protect patients from harm (including emotional/psychological harm)
- The charge nurse failed in her duty by laughing instead of correcting the behavior
- Reporting was done through proper channels (manager)
- Patient advocacy is a core ethical principle in healthcare
- The behavior created a hostile environment for the patient
- Retaliation doesn't change the morality of the original reporting action

- Might have escalated too quickly (but the context suggests this was serious)
- Created workplace conflict (but this is a consequence, not a moral failing)

The key ethical principles at play:
- **Beneficence/Non-maleficence**: Protecting the patient from harm
- **Patient dignity**: The comments dehumanized the patient
- **Professional standards**: Healthcare workers must maintain professionalism
- **Whistleblower protection**: Reporting misconduct is generally protected and encouraged
- **Justice**: Holding people accountable for wrongdoing

The retaliation from the nurse's friend group is unfortunate but doesn't make the original action wrong. In fact, it suggests a toxic workplace culture that needs addressing.
